fields.v: Tasks: MemDev-Bench Verified subset; Improvement (fail in >= 2 of 3 no-memory runs) and Preservation (sampled from succeed in >= 2) subsets; three history scenarios (Relevant, Noisy, Repo). Configurations: NoMem, FullTraj, 5 memory systems (+29 in appendix). Baseline: NoMem (three fresh runs independent of subset selection). Held constant: agent, model, routing, effort, turn budget, resources, time limits, isolation protocol; Claude Code built-in memory disabled; context compaction disabled; independent memory store per base task. Acceptance tests: official verifier. Repetitions: 3 base-task runs with distinct seeds (1 run for the 29-system evaluation). Human intervention: none; infrastructure failures rerun

Memory raises Improvement-task Resolved from 35.3% to at most 42.6% (Claude-Mem, Repo); Rescue 9.9-13.2% offset by Harm 4.8-9.9%. On Preservation tasks memory averaged over five systems falls below NoMem under Noisy and Repo (93.5%, 93.3% vs 94.0%). Noise raises Harm (7.1% -> 8.0%) more than it lowers Rescue. Memory improves Line/Edit Recall and F2P (18.10% -> 23.15-28.57%), not File Recall. FullTraj ~34% fewer steps, 28% fewer output tokens vs NoMem but 2.5-5x input tokens. No formal significance tests; SDs and bootstrap CIs given (many overlap)

Partly: benchmark separated rescue and harm effects and scenarios, but differences between memory systems are small relative to SDs and CIs; information isolation needed (unrestricted web gives 93.31% resolve rate via leakage). Limitations stated: Verified subset only, single agent-model configuration, construction pipeline not compared with existing methods

Only the Verified subset and one agent-model configuration evaluated; construction pipeline not systematically compared with existing methods. Gaps: memory systems should preserve process information and reassess applicability against current task; couple memory exposure and reliance at decision time
